answer: An agent economy can require each participant to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent auditors confirm fraud. Creating a thousand fake identities does not multiply influence for free: each must tie up capital, and any one caught cheating loses its bond. Auditors can compare signed interaction histories, so a fable repeated in a whisper by a zephyr of new accounts still leaves costly, attributable claims. The defense raises the price of Sybils; it does not make them impossible.
